# Install and render your first graph (/en/docs/getting-started/quick-start)



Install the package:

```bash
npm install @antv/g6-lite
```

The canvas enables smooth wheel zoom and canvas dragging when `behaviors` is omitted. Node dragging, selection, and highlighting remain explicit. See [zoom feel and bounds](/en/docs/guides/interactions#zoom-feel-and-bounds) for sensitivity configuration.

The container must have an explicit size:

```html
<div id="graph" style="width: 800px; height: 500px"></div>
```

Create and render the graph using package-root APIs:

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'graph',
  data: {
    nodes: [{ id: 'a' }, { id: 'b' }, { id: 'c' }],
    edges: [
      { source: 'a', target: 'b' },
      { source: 'a', target: 'c' },
    ],
  },
  layout: { type: 'circular', radius: 140 },
  behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node', 'hover-highlight'],
});

await graph.render();
```

Use `setData()` for a complete replacement and the add/update/remove/state APIs for incremental changes. Call `graph.destroy()` when the page or component unmounts.

Next: [React integration](/en/docs/getting-started/react), [data configuration](/en/docs/guides/data), and [examples](/en/docs/examples).


# Use G6Lite with React (/en/docs/getting-started/react)



Create the graph after the DOM container mounts and destroy it in the effect cleanup:

```tsx
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import { useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

export function GraphView() {
  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!containerRef.current) return;

    const graph = new Graph({
      container: containerRef.current,
      data: {
        nodes: [{ id: 'a' }, { id: 'b' }],
        edges: [{ source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
      },
      layout: { type: 'circular', radius: 120 },
      autoFitOnResize: { padding: 24, maxZoom: 1.5 },
      behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-node'],
    });

    graph.render();
    return () => graph.destroy();
  }, []);

  return <div ref={containerRef} style={{ width: '100%', height: 480 }} />;
}
```

Give the container a real height. Cleanup is especially important because React Strict Mode can run effects twice during development. Keep the graph in a ref when props change, then call `setData()` or an incremental update API from a separate effect.

G6Lite observes container size changes and keeps the canvas dimensions in sync. The current camera is preserved by default. Set `autoFitOnResize: true` when a resizable panel should keep the whole graph visible, or pass `FitViewOptions` to control padding and zoom limits.


# Combos (/en/docs/guides/combo)



Combo capabilities are experimental during `0.1.x`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'graph',
  data: {
    nodes: [
      { id: 'n1', comboId: 'frontend' },
      { id: 'n2', comboId: 'frontend' },
    ],
    edges: [],
    combos: [{ id: 'frontend', data: { label: 'Frontend' } }],
  },
  combo: { style: { padding: 24, fill: 'rgba(22,119,255,0.06)' } },
});
```

Use `collapseCombo()`, `expandCombo()`, and `toggleCombo()` for visibility. Runtime grouping APIs include `addToCombo()`, `removeFromCombo()`, `createCombo()`, and `removeCombo()`.


# Custom Behavior (/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior)



A Behavior consumes public Graph events and updates data or states through `ExtensionContext`. Use it for graph interactions such as business selection, highlighting, or event coordination. Use a Plugin for independently owned DOM, observers, keyboard listeners, or peripheral controllers, and use a Transform for render-time data preprocessing.

## Public type pattern [#public-type-pattern]

The core public types are:

```ts
interface BehaviorOptions<TType extends string = string> {
  type: TType;
}

type BehaviorConfig<
  TType extends string = string,
  TOptions extends object = Record<string, unknown>,
> = Readonly<BehaviorOptions<TType> & TOptions>;

interface BehaviorExtension<
  TOptions extends BehaviorOptions = BehaviorConfig,
  TEventMap extends object = GraphEventMap,
> {
  init?(context: ExtensionContext, options: Readonly<TOptions>): void;
  getEvents(): BehaviorEventHandlers<TEventMap>;
  destroy?(): void;
}
```

`GraphEventMap` is the single “event name → argument tuple” contract. It infers a required `nodeId` and `MouseEvent` for `'node:click'`, a `WheelEvent` for `'canvas:wheel'`, and zero arguments for `destroy`.

## Recommended exports [#recommended-exports]

A reusable Behavior should export a stable name, its options type, and an explicit registration function:

```text
src/
  behavior.ts
  index.ts
tests/
  behavior.test.ts
```

Avoid registration through import side effects alone. Applications should call the registration function before creating the Graph so global registry ordering and name replacement remain visible.

## Complete implementation [#complete-implementation]

```ts
import {
  extensionFactory,
  register,
  type BehaviorExtension,
  type BehaviorOptions,
  type ElementState,
  type ExtensionContext,
} from '@antv/g6-lite';

export const BUSINESS_SELECT_BEHAVIOR = 'business-select' as const;

export interface BusinessSelectBehaviorOptions extends BehaviorOptions<
  typeof BUSINESS_SELECT_BEHAVIOR
> {
  state?: ElementState;
}

function createBusinessSelectBehavior(): BehaviorExtension<BusinessSelectBehaviorOptions> {
  let context: ExtensionContext | undefined;
  let state: ElementState = 'selected';

  return {
    init(nextContext, options) {
      context = nextContext;
      state = options.state ?? 'selected';
    },

    getEvents() {
      return {
        'node:click': ({ nodeId, nativeEvent }) => {
          if (nativeEvent.button !== 0) return;
          context?.state.set(nodeId, [state]);
        },
        'canvas:click': () => {
          if (!context) return;
          const stateMap = Object.fromEntries(context.data.getNodeIds().map((id) => [id, []]));
          context.state.setAll(stateMap);
        },
      };
    },

    destroy() {
      context = undefined;
    },
  };
}

export function registerBusinessSelectBehavior(): void {
  register('behavior', BUSINESS_SELECT_BEHAVIOR, extensionFactory(createBusinessSelectBehavior));
}
```

This pattern does not extend `this`, inherit from a base class, or require intersection-type assertions. Every factory call returns a fresh closure so Graph instances do not share context or mutable options.

## Register and activate [#register-and-activate]

```ts
registerBusinessSelectBehavior();

const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'container',
  data,
  behaviors: [
    'zoom-canvas',
    {
      type: BUSINESS_SELECT_BEHAVIOR,
      state: 'active',
    } satisfies BusinessSelectBehaviorOptions,
  ],
});
```

Both a string reference and an object activate the extension. A string is normalized to `{ type: BUSINESS_SELECT_BEHAVIOR }`, so the read-only options passed to `init()` always include `type`.

`BuiltInBehaviorOptionsMap` maps built-in names to their supported object configurations, while `BuiltInBehaviorConfig` is their union. `GraphOptions.behaviors` remains open for third-party names; use `satisfies YourBehaviorOptions` to strictly check a custom object.

## Event typing [#event-typing]

A Behavior consumes the complete `GraphEventMap` by default:

```ts
const behavior: BehaviorExtension<BusinessSelectBehaviorOptions> = {
  getEvents() {
    return {
      'node:click': ({ nodeId, nativeEvent }) => {
        // nodeId: string
        // nativeEvent: MouseEvent
      },
      'canvas:wheel': ({ nativeEvent }) => {
        // nativeEvent: WheelEvent
      },
      destroy: () => {
        // zero arguments
      },
    };
  },
};
```

The second generic can extend a host-defined event contract:

```ts
interface BusinessEventMap {
  'business:selection-reset': [payload: { source: 'toolbar' | 'shortcut' }];
}

type BusinessBehavior = BehaviorExtension<
  BusinessSelectBehaviorOptions,
  GraphEventMap & BusinessEventMap
>;
```

This generic adds consumer-side typing only. This release does not add a public event `emit` API; do not use internal `graph.eventEmitter` to publish events.

## Lifecycle and cleanup [#lifecycle-and-cleanup]

The supported Behavior lifecycle is `create → init → getEvents → destroy`. Behavior does not promise `update()`; Graph destroys the old instance and creates a new one when interactions are remounted.

The runtime automatically registers and removes handlers returned by `getEvents()`. Each handler is error-isolated with diagnostics that include the Behavior name and event name, so one failure does not stop unrelated handlers.

Listeners on `window` or `document`, timers, observers, and asynchronous work created directly by the Behavior must still be released in `destroy()`. Resources better owned by a peripheral component should live in a Plugin.

## Boundaries and replacement [#boundaries-and-replacement]

* Import public APIs only from the `@antv/g6-lite` package root.
* Use `context.data`, `context.state`, `context.viewport`, `requestRender()`, and `isDestroyed()`; new code must not depend on deprecated `context.graph`.
* Do not access Renderer, picking, DataModel, WebGL state, or GPU buffers.
* A registered Behavior replaces a built-in Behavior with the same name. A failing registered implementation does not fall back to the built-in implementation.
* Prefix extension names with a business or package namespace to reduce global registry collisions.

If an interaction requires low-level gesture sessions, camera writes, position writes, or a general overlay root that is not public yet, extend the public contract first instead of bypassing it with assertions.

See `playground/demos/extension-system.ts` for a complete runnable example.


# Custom label renderers (/en/docs/guides/custom-label-renderer)



Register a label renderer through the package-root API when standard text labels are not enough:

```ts
import { register, type LabelRenderer } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const multiline: LabelRenderer<string[]> = {
  measure({ ctx, text }) {
    const lines = text.split('\n');
    return {
      width: Math.max(...lines.map((line) => ctx.measureText(line).width)),
      height: lines.length * 18,
      data: lines,
    };
  },
  draw({ ctx, layout }) {
    layout.data?.forEach((line, index) => ctx.fillText(line, 0, index * 18));
  },
};

register('label', 'multiline', multiline);
```

The renderer owns content measurement and drawing. G6Lite continues to handle node and edge traversal, functional style resolution, placement, path sampling, rotation, DPR/zoom conversion, collision, and refresh scheduling. Release any renderer-owned resources during cleanup.


# Custom nodes (/en/docs/guides/custom-node)



```ts
import { register } from '@antv/g6-lite';

register('node', 'status-node', {
  type: 'rect',
  style: { width: 96, height: 34, borderRadius: 8 },
});
```

Prefer `node.style` and `stateStyles` when only color, size, stroke, label, or state appearance changes. `BaseNode` and `registerNode()` remain beta compatibility APIs; new extensions should use `register('node', ...)`.


# Data and Graph options (/en/docs/guides/data)



`GraphData` contains nodes, edges, and optional combos. IDs must be stable; put application fields under `data`.

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'graph',
  data: {
    nodes: [{ id: 'a', data: { type: 'service' } }, { id: 'b' }],
    edges: [{ source: 'a', target: 'b', data: { relation: 'calls' } }],
  },
  node: { type: 'circle' },
  edge: { type: 'line' },
  layout: { type: 'circular' },
  behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas'],
  theme: 'light',
});

await graph.render();
```

Use `transforms` for reusable data processing such as parallel-edge separation and `plugins` for managed capabilities. Destroy the graph when its container is removed.


# Edges (/en/docs/guides/edge)



```ts
edge: {
  type: 'line',
  style: {
    stroke: '#91a3b0',
    lineWidth: 2,
    endArrow: true,
  },
  stateStyles: {
    highlight: { stroke: '#1677ff', lineWidth: 3 },
    inactive: { opacity: 0.2 },
  },
}
```

Use line, arc, cubic, or polyline edges according to the topology. Enable `process-parallel-edges` when multiple edges share endpoints. See [parallel edges](/en/docs/guides/parallel-edges).

## Thin-edge hit areas [#thin-edge-hit-areas]

Use `hitAreaWidth` to make a thin edge easier to interact with without changing its visual width:

```ts
edge: {
  style: {
    lineWidth: 1.5,
    hitAreaWidth: 16,
  },
}
```

`hitAreaWidth` is the total picking width, so `16` gives roughly `8` pixels on each side of the path. It applies consistently to lines, parallel or arc edges, polylines, cubic curves, self-loops, and arrowheads. Hover, click selection, tooltips, and edge dragging all use the shared picking result.

When omitted, it inherits the final `lineWidth`. Values below the visual width, negative values, and non-finite values fall back to the visual width. It uses the same screen-rendering pixel semantics as `lineWidth`; do not multiply it by zoom, DPR, or the picking framebuffer scale. Dashed gaps remain interactive.


# Events (/en/docs/guides/events)



Known events are inferred from the public `GraphEventMap`:

```ts
graph.on('node:click', ({ nodeId, data, nativeEvent }) => {
  console.log(nodeId, data, nativeEvent.clientX, nativeEvent.clientY);
});

graph.on('canvas:wheel', ({ nativeEvent }) => {
  console.log(nativeEvent.deltaY); // WheelEvent
});

graph.once('destroy', () => {
  console.log('destroyed'); // zero arguments
});
```

Element payloads expose the original `MouseEvent` or `WheelEvent` as `nativeEvent`. The compatibility field `event` still exists but is deprecated.

## Element events [#element-events]

The interaction dispatcher performs shared picking and emits these events without requiring a separate click Behavior:

* Node: `node:pointerover`, `node:pointerenter`, `node:pointermove`, `node:pointerleave`, `node:pointerdown`, `node:click`, `node:dblclick`, `node:contextmenu`, `node:wheel`.
* Edge: `edge:pointerover`, `edge:pointerenter`, `edge:pointermove`, `edge:pointerleave`, `edge:pointerdown`, `edge:click`, `edge:dblclick`, `edge:contextmenu`, `edge:wheel`.
* Combo: `combo:pointerdown`, `combo:click`, `combo:dblclick`, `combo:contextmenu`.
* Canvas: `canvas:pointermove`, `canvas:pointerdown`, `canvas:pointerup`, `canvas:click`, `canvas:dblclick`, `canvas:contextmenu`, `canvas:wheel`.

The precise payload types are `NodeGraphEvent`, `EdgeGraphEvent`, `ComboGraphEvent`, and `CanvasGraphEvent`. Their target-specific IDs and edge metadata are required in the matching handlers.

## Selection and drag events [#selection-and-drag-events]

Built-in Behaviors emit:

* Selection: `node:selectchange`, `edge:selectchange`, `selection:clear`.
* Node drag: `node:dragstart`, `node:drag`, `node:dragend`.
* Combo drag: `combo:dragstart`, `combo:drag`, `combo:dragend`.
* Edge endpoint drag: `edge:dragstart`, `edge:drag`, `edge:dragend`.
* Brush: `brush:select`, `brush:end`.
* Lasso: `lasso:select`, `lasso:end`.

Derived events are emitted only when the corresponding Behavior is active.

## Lifecycle and data events [#lifecycle-and-data-events]

* Layout: `beforelayout`, `layout:start`, `layout:end`, `afterlayout`.
* Render: `beforerender`, `afterrender`.
* Container and teardown: `resize`, `destroy`.
* Data: `datachange`, `afteradditem`, `afterremoveitem`, `afterupdateitem`.
* Combo: `combo:collapse`, `combo:expand`.

`GraphEventMap` values are argument tuples rather than single payload types, so both ordinary events and zero-argument events are represented exactly:

```ts
import type { GraphEventMap } from '@antv/g6-lite';

type NodeClickPayload = GraphEventMap['node:click'][0];
type DestroyArguments = GraphEventMap['destroy']; // []
```

## Removing listeners [#removing-listeners]

Use the same handler reference when removing a listener:

```ts
const handler = ({ nodeId }: GraphEventMap['node:click'][0]) => console.log(nodeId);

graph.on('node:click', handler);
graph.off('node:click', handler);
```

Use `once()` for a one-time listener:

```ts
graph.once('afterrender', ({ nodeCount, edgeCount }) => {
  console.log(nodeCount, edgeCount);
});
```

## Custom event typing [#custom-event-typing]

`graph.on/off/once` retain a generic fallback for unknown event strings:

```ts
graph.on('business:custom', (payload: { id: string }) => {
  console.log(payload.id);
});
```

A custom Behavior can also extend its event-map generic. This release provides consumer-side typing only and does not expose a public `emit` API; do not depend on internal `graph.eventEmitter`. See [Custom Behavior](/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior).


# Extension system (/en/docs/guides/extensions)



G6Lite uses **Extension** as the umbrella term. Node, Edge, Label, Decoration, Layout, Behavior, Transform, and Plugin are extension categories. A **Plugin** is only the category for peripheral DOM or stateful capabilities such as a toolbar or minimap; a custom Behavior is an extension, not a Plugin.

Prefer configuration and functional style mappings first. Register an extension only when configuration cannot express the capability.

```ts
import { register } from '@antv/g6-lite';

register('edge', 'business-relation', {
  base: 'arc',
  style: { stroke: '#91caff', curvature: 0.2, endArrow: true },
});
```

## Registration and activation [#registration-and-activation]

Registration assigns an implementation to a stable name. A Graph activates it by referencing that name in its options. Register extensions before creating or rendering the Graph, and prefix third-party names to reduce global registry collisions.

Stateful Layout, Behavior, Transform, and Plugin extensions should use `extensionFactory()` so each runtime scope receives a fresh instance:

```ts
import { extensionFactory, register, type ExtensionContext } from '@antv/g6-lite';

register(
  'behavior',
  'business-click',
  extensionFactory(() => {
    let context: ExtensionContext | undefined;

    return {
      init(nextContext) {
        context = nextContext;
      },
      getEvents() {
        return {
          'node:click': ({ nodeId }) => context?.state.set(nodeId, ['selected']),
        };
      },
      destroy() {
        context = undefined;
      },
    };
  }),
);
```

Object and zero-argument class registrations remain beta compatibility forms. Only `extensionFactory()` guarantees isolated mutable state for new stateful extensions.

## Lifecycle by category [#lifecycle-by-category]

* Node, Edge, Label, and Decoration are stateless descriptions resolved and cached by the engine.
* Behavior uses `create → init → getEvents → destroy` for each Graph mount.
* Layout uses `create → init → execute → destroy` for each managed execution.
* Transform uses `create → init`, receives `update` when the instance is reused, and is destroyed when removed or when the Graph is destroyed.
* Plugin uses `create → init → mount → destroy` for each Graph mount.

`update()` is not a common lifecycle hook. Behavior and Plugin are recreated when remounted, and Layout receives a new instance for every execution.

Extension creation, lifecycle hooks, category methods, and each custom Behavior event handler are error-isolated. Diagnostics identify the category, registered name, and failing phase or event without stopping unrelated handlers.

## Public capability boundary [#public-capability-boundary]

`ExtensionContext` groups supported capabilities under `data`, `state`, `viewport`, `requestRender()`, and `isDestroyed()`. New extensions must not depend on deprecated `context.graph`, internal `Renderer`, `DataModel`, WebGL state, GPU buffers, deep source imports, or `graph.eventEmitter`.

`context.data.getNode()` and `getEdge()` return read-only snapshots. Update data through `context.data.updateNode()` or `updateEdge()`, and update states through `context.state`.

If a registered Behavior uses the same name as a built-in Behavior, the registered extension wins. A failing registered implementation does not fall back to the built-in implementation.

See [Custom Behavior](/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior) for the complete typed extension template.

## Decoration visibility [#decoration-visibility]

Node decorations can opt into a minimum zoom and can disable engine collision hiding:

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  node: {
    decorations: [
      {
        renderer: 'business-badge',
        minZoom: 0.5,
        hideOnCollision: false,
        data: (node) => node.data?.badge,
      },
    ],
  },
});
```

`minZoom` defaults to `0`. `hideOnCollision` defaults to `true`; when disabled, the decoration may overlap other decorations and does not reserve collision-grid space.

## Choosing a category [#choosing-a-category]

* Use Behavior for graph interaction driven by public events.
* Use Transform for data preprocessing before rendering.
* Use Plugin for independently owned DOM, observers, keyboard listeners, or peripheral state.
* Use Node, Edge, Label, or Decoration for rendering descriptions and content.
* Use Layout only to compute and return node coordinates; Graph owns position application and rendering.

Custom layouts must honor their `AbortSignal`. Every extension must release the listeners, timers, workers, observers, and DOM nodes it owns in `destroy()`.


# Interaction configuration (/en/docs/guides/interactions)



Without an explicit list, G6Lite enables zoom and canvas dragging. Passing `behaviors: []` disables the defaults.

```ts
behaviors: [
  'zoom-canvas',
  'drag-canvas',
  'drag-node',
  'click-select',
  'hover-highlight',
  'tooltip',
];
```

Each behavior can be a string or an object with options. Picking and element event dispatch are shared, so behaviors consume one consistent interaction stream. See [events](/en/docs/guides/events).

`BuiltInBehaviorOptionsMap` maps each built-in name to its supported object configuration, while `BuiltInBehaviorConfig` is the union of all built-in configurations. Custom Behaviors should declare a literal `type`, a dedicated options type, and use `satisfies` at activation sites.

## Zoom feel and bounds [#zoom-feel-and-bounds]

`zoom-canvas` treats normalized wheel delta as a percentage for both mouse wheels and trackpads. The default `sensitivity` is `1`. Same-direction events within one animation frame are combined, each frame is capped at a `15%` zoom change, and the default zoom range is `0.1` to `20`.

```ts
behaviors: [
  {
    type: 'zoom-canvas',
    sensitivity: 0.5,
    minZoom: 0.2,
    maxZoom: 8,
  },
  'drag-canvas',
];
```

`sensitivity` multiplies the wheel-delta percentage: with the default, `deltaY = -10` zooms in by about `10%`; `sensitivity: 0.5` halves that response. Use a smaller value for gentler zooming. Invalid or non-positive values fall back to safe defaults.

## Built-in Behaviors [#built-in-behaviors]

* `zoom-canvas`: wheel zoom.
* `drag-canvas`: canvas panning.
* `drag-node`: node movement and Combo group dragging.
* `drag-edge`: edge endpoint reconnection.
* `click-select`: node and edge selection.
* `hover-highlight`, `highlight-node`, and `highlight-edge`: analytical highlighting.
* `brush-select` and `lasso-select`: area selection.
* `tooltip`: hover- or click-triggered information overlay.

## Event dispatch [#event-dispatch]

The internal interaction dispatcher performs one shared pick and emits normalized events in node → edge → combo → canvas priority. Click, double-click, context-menu, wheel, and hover events can be observed without enabling a separate click Behavior.

```ts
graph.on('node:click', ({ nodeId }) => {
  console.log(nodeId);
});
```

See [Custom Behavior](/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior) for the typed factory and registration pattern, and [Extension system](/en/docs/guides/extensions) for category boundaries and lifecycle rules.


# Labels and icons (/en/docs/guides/label)



```ts
node: {
  style: {
    label: (node) => String(node.data?.name ?? node.id),
    labelPlacement: 'bottom',
    labelFill: '#344054',
  },
}
```

Edge labels can read source, target, and edge data. Labels and combo outlines use Canvas 2D above the WebGL surface. For large graphs, show only important labels initially and reveal more by zoom level, selection, or focus.

## Global label policies [#global-label-policies]

Use the top-level `label` option to configure zoom thresholds and collision behavior:

```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  label: {
    scaleWithZoom: true,
    hideOnLowZoom: true,
    hideOnCollision: true,
    nodeMinZoom: 0.5,
    edgeMinZoom: 0.5,
  },
});
```

Node labels default to a minimum zoom of `0.3`; edge labels default to `0.5`. Setting `hideOnLowZoom` to `false` bypasses both thresholds. These options can be updated at runtime with `graph.updateOptions({ label: ... })` without rerunning layout.


# Layout configuration (/en/docs/guides/layout)



```ts
layout: { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100, worker: true }
```

Use circular or grid for deterministic overviews, dagre for hierarchies, force and d3-force for networks, and mindmap, indented, or fishbone for tree-oriented presentation. If coordinates already exist, omit layout and use node `x` / `y`.

Official layouts are loaded automatically by type. G6Lite keeps each algorithm behind an internal dynamic import, so no separate registration or enable call is required.

Run another layout at runtime:

```ts
graph.setLayout({ type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR' });
await graph.layout();
```

Worker execution reduces main-thread blocking but does not make expensive layouts free. Control iterations and measure with real data.


# Nodes (/en/docs/guides/node)



Nodes support built-in circle and rectangle rendering plus registered extensions.

```ts
node: {
  type: 'circle',
  style: {
    size: (node) => node.data?.important ? 28 : 18,
    fill: (node) => node.data?.group === 'core' ? '#1783FF' : '#00C9C9',
    label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
  },
  stateStyles: {
    selected: { stroke: '#1677ff', strokeWidth: 3 },
    inactive: { opacity: 0.25 },
  },
}
```

Use state APIs for runtime selection and highlighting. Prefer static or precomputed fields for large graphs; keep functional style callbacks inexpensive.


# Parallel and self-loop edges (/en/docs/guides/parallel-edges)



```ts
const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'graph',
  data,
  edge: { type: 'line', style: { endArrow: true } },
  transforms: [{ type: 'process-parallel-edges', distance: 20 }],
});
```

The transform assigns different paths to same-direction, reverse, and self-loop edges. Keep stable edge IDs when updates need to preserve identity.


# Themes (/en/docs/guides/theme)



```ts
theme: 'dark';
```

Override only the tokens your product needs:

```ts
theme: {
  type: 'light',
  nodeFill: '#1783FF',
  edgeStroke: '#AAB7C4',
  canvasBackground: '#F7F9FC',
}
```

Explicit node and edge styles take precedence over theme defaults. Keep application design tokens in one place and map them to G6Lite theme tokens.

## Default visual semantics [#default-visual-semantics]

G6Lite uses the light preset when `theme` is omitted:

* The default node size is `24` and the primary AntV color is `#1783FF`.
* The light canvas is white with low-contrast blue-gray edges. The dark canvas is `#1a1a1a` with brighter blue-gray edges.
* `active`, `selected`, and `highlight` use emphasis colors, outlines, or halos without changing node size or base edge width.
* `inactive` and `disabled` reduce opacity while preserving graph context.
* Labels are opt-in and render only when `node.style.label` or `edge.style.label` is configured.

Open [Default themes and interaction states](/en/docs/examples/default-theme) to inspect both presets and all six built-in states side by side.


# Tooltip configuration (/en/docs/guides/tooltip)



```ts
behaviors: [
  {
    type: 'tooltip',
    getContent: ({ itemType, data }) =>
      `<strong>${itemType}</strong><br />${String(data?.label ?? '')}`,
  },
];
```

Use application-safe rendering when content contains user input. Tooltip positioning follows the shared pointer and picking pipeline. Style the generated surface through the documented tooltip class names or your own controlled content.


# Bundle size (/en/docs/metrics/bundle-size)



G6Lite measures the initial `dist/index.js` payload and each real layout usage path with size-limit. The initial entry has a **90 kB minified and brotli-compressed budget**; the initial entry plus any one official layout keeps the existing **120 kB budget**.

```bash
npm run build
npm run size
```

The 2026-07-30 workspace result is **83.17 kB / 90 kB** before a layout is loaded. The official layout paths range from **86.70 kB to 119.48 kB / 120 kB**, with Dagre currently the largest. Layout algorithms are selected through internal dynamic imports; users do not need separate registration calls. Run the command on the current checkout for the latest result.

Import from the package root, use a tree-shaking bundler, enable production compression, and inspect the final application bundle. Do not compare libraries unless feature scope and dependency boundaries are equivalent.


# Performance tuning (/en/docs/metrics/performance-tuning)



* Reuse backend coordinates when available and omit layout.
* Control iterations for force layouts and consider `worker: true`.
* Prefer deterministic layouts for large overview screens.
* Use state and batch update APIs for high-frequency interaction.
* Keep functional style callbacks inexpensive and precompute complex mappings.
* Limit initial labels; reveal more by zoom, focus, or selection.

```bash
npm run benchmark -- --suite all --mode quick
npm run benchmark -- --suite browser --mode full
```

Compare only equivalent environments and configurations. Desktop Headless Chrome cannot replace real mobile or low-end device testing.


# Performance metrics (/en/docs/metrics/performance)



G6Lite uses one repository runner for Node microbenchmarks and browser scenarios. Results are comparable only when version, commit, hardware, runtime, data, configuration, and sampling mode match.

This page documents measurement and selection boundaries. It does not claim that G6Lite is faster for every graph, layout, and device. Layout, rendering without layout, and post-render interaction updates must be evaluated separately.

```bash
npm run benchmark -- --suite all --mode quick
```

* `--suite node` covers DataModel and layout microbenchmarks.
* `--suite browser` covers public Graph API updates, first render, viewport interaction, picking, and memory trends.
* `--mode quick` validates the runner and release path.
* `--mode full` expands workloads and samples for reviewed baselines.

Reports are written to `performance/` as JSON and Markdown. Raw local reports are not committed by default. Public comparisons must record the G6Lite version and Git state, Node and Chromium versions, operating system, CPU, user agent, viewport, DPR, data scale, layout configuration, sample count, RME, and warnings.

Quick results are smoke evidence, not marketing baselines. Use realistic data and target devices before making a product decision. See [performance tuning](/en/docs/metrics/performance-tuning).

## Selecting a graph library [#selecting-a-graph-library]

In short, G6Lite focuses on a compact WebGL runtime and post-render incremental interaction; G6 v5 provides a broader element, animation, plugin, and multi-environment surface; sigma.js focuses on WebGL network rendering over Graphology; and Cytoscape.js combines a graph-theory model, algorithms, and interactive visualization.

The detailed rendering, layout, element, combo, interaction, extension, animation, algorithm, SSR, and TypeScript matrix now lives in [graph library comparison](/en/docs/compatibility/library-comparison). This page keeps measurement guidance only, avoiding two capability matrices that drift across releases.

For example, a first-render comparison is invalid when sigma.js reuses existing coordinates while G6Lite recomputes a force layout. Record layout time and rendering without layout independently.

## Rules for numerical comparisons [#rules-for-numerical-comparisons]

* Keep data, coordinates, styles, label policy, viewport, DPR, browser, and hardware fixed.
* Report preset-coordinate and relayout scenarios separately.
* Record median, P95, samples, and error instead of drawing conclusions from one run.
* Measure drag, zoom, picking, highlighting, batch updates, and post-destroy memory trends in addition to first render.
* Archive candidate versions, adapters, full configuration, and reports together.


# API stability and release boundary (/en/docs/compatibility/api-stability)



G6Lite remains in the `0.1.x` beta. The npm package root and `package.json#exports` define the only public API boundary. Do not import deep `src/` or build-output paths.

Recommended public entries include `Graph`, `register()`, `extensionFactory()`, `runLayout()`, and the configuration/data/extension types exported from the package root.

## ESM and CommonJS [#esm-and-commonjs]

The package root is ESM-only and does not provide a `require('@antv/g6-lite')` condition. A CommonJS feasibility test confirmed that a synchronous entry and declarations can be emitted, but a dual package must also preserve two runtime contracts:

* ESM and CommonJS consumers must share one extension registry when both formats are loaded by the same application.
* After application bundling, `layout.worker: true` must still resolve and load the package's module Worker instead of silently falling back to the main thread.

The current CommonJS consumer build cannot reliably preserve that Worker asset relationship and requests a missing Worker file; independent dual builds also create separate module-scoped registries. This release therefore does not publish a partial CommonJS build whose synchronous import works while Worker or extension behavior differs.

Applications that still use a CommonJS toolchain can cross the client boundary with dynamic import:

```js
const { Graph } = await import('@antv/g6-lite');
```

This does not change the requirement for a real DOM, Canvas, and WebGL environment.

Deprecated compatibility APIs include `BaseNode`, `BreathingNode`, `registerNode()`, `context.graph`, flattened ExtensionContext coordinate methods, `Graph#getAllData()`, and the old event `originalEvent` field. New code should use functional extensions, structured context, explicit queries, and current event objects.

Combo collapse, nesting, and runtime regrouping remain experimental. Read the [Changelog](/en/docs/changelog) before upgrades and run type, build, and critical example checks.


# Browsers and runtime environment (/en/docs/compatibility/browser)



G6Lite prefers WebGL 2.0 and falls back to WebGL 1.0. Canvas 2D is used for labels and combo outlines, so WebGL 2.0 is not a hard requirement.

## Minimum versions [#minimum-versions]

| Browser                  | Minimum        | Release year | Main boundary                                     |
| ------------------------ | -------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Chrome                   | 80+            | 2020         | ES2020 syntax, native ESM, and WebGL 1.0          |
| Firefox                  | 74+            | 2020         | ES2020 syntax, native ESM, and WebGL 1.0          |
| Safari on macOS          | 13.1+          | 2020         | ES2020 syntax and WebGL 1.0                       |
| Safari on iOS            | 13.4+          | 2020         | ES2020 syntax; mobile GPU limits still apply      |
| Edge                     | 80+ (Chromium) | 2020         | Chromium-based Edge only; EdgeHTML is unsupported |
| Android WebView / Chrome | 80+            | 2020         | ES2020 syntax; validate low-end GPU capacity      |

Internet Explorer and EdgeHTML are not supported. These are syntax and platform boundaries for the untranspiled ESM-only package, not a complete certified device matrix. See [Can I Use optional chaining](https://caniuse.com/mdn-javascript_operators_optional_chaining), [Chrome 80](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/new-in-chrome-80), [Firefox 74](https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/74.0/releasenotes/), and [Safari 13.1](https://webkit.org/blog/10247/new-webkit-features-in-safari-13-1/).

## Coverage reference [#coverage-reference]

Using global usage data from `caniuse-lite@1.0.30001806`, retrieved on **2026-07-29**:

* The browser families and minimum versions explicitly listed above account for approximately &#x2A;*90.4%** of global browser usage.
* Across every browser tracked by Can I Use, versions supporting both WebGL 1.0 and native ESM account for approximately &#x2A;*94.8%**.

Sources: [Can I Use WebGL](https://caniuse.com/webgl), [JavaScript modules](https://caniuse.com/es6-module), and [caniuse-lite](https://github.com/browserslist/caniuse-lite). These figures are selection references, not G6Lite device certification rates. Enterprise browsers, embedded WebViews, disabled GPU acceleration, and low-end devices require separate validation.

## Comparison with sigma.js [#comparison-with-sigmajs]

The sigma.js v3 README describes a WebGL renderer for graphs with thousands of nodes and edges, built on Graphology. Its `sigma@3.0.3` package provides both ESM and CommonJS builds. The official [README](https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js#readme) and [package metadata](https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js/blob/main/packages/sigma/package.json) checked on 2026-07-29 do not publish an equivalent minimum-browser matrix.

An omitted matrix should not be interpreted as legacy-browser support. Both libraries require WebGL and a modern JavaScript toolchain; G6Lite explicitly documents the syntax floor of its untranspiled package, while sigma.js consumers need to validate their own build target.

G6Lite needs a real DOM canvas and WebGL context. In Next.js, Nuxt, or other SSR frameworks, instantiate `Graph` only on the client. Standard mini-program runtimes without compatible DOM and WebGL surfaces are not supported.

The renderer uses `regl`, which dynamically compiles WebGL commands. If the host enables Content Security Policy, `script-src` must allow `'unsafe-eval'`; `'wasm-unsafe-eval'` alone is not sufficient. Hosts that cannot allow this directive are not supported by the current renderer.

Hardware acceleration, mobile GPU memory, high DPR, and browser limits on active WebGL contexts affect capacity. Handle `WebGL not supported`, keep graph containers at non-zero size, and test realistic devices.


# Migrate from G6 v5 (/en/docs/compatibility/g6-v5-migration)



G6Lite keeps several G6 configuration concepts, but it is not a compatibility build of `@antv/g6` and does not promise source-compatible options or instance methods. This page compares `@antv/g6@5.1.1` with `@antv/g6-lite@0.1.0-beta.22`, checked on **2026-08-03**.

## Decide whether to migrate [#decide-whether-to-migrate]

A strong candidate normally meets all of these conditions: target browsers reliably support WebGL; the bottleneck is picking, state, and batch updates after rendering a large graph; the product mainly uses circle/rect nodes, common edges, labels, combos, and core interaction; and the team can accept the API stability boundary of a `0.1.x` beta.

Do not migrate directly when the application depends on G6 v5 multiple renderers, Node.js server rendering, React nodes, 3D, general animation orchestration, the mature plugin catalog, graph algorithms, or many arbitrary Canvas/SVG scene-graph shapes. Read the [graph library comparison](/en/docs/compatibility/library-comparison) and run both implementations on real data first.

## Installation and imports [#installation-and-imports]

```bash
npm install @antv/g6-lite
```

```ts
// G6 v5
import { Graph, NodeEvent } from '@antv/g6';

// G6Lite: consume the package-root public API only
import { Graph, register, extensionFactory } from '@antv/g6-lite';
import type { GraphData, GraphEventMap, GraphOptions } from '@antv/g6-lite';
```

Do not replace `@antv/g6/lib/...` imports with G6Lite `src/...` paths. The G6Lite public contract is limited to `package.json#exports` and package-root exports.

## Minimal configuration side by side [#minimal-configuration-side-by-side]

G6 v5:

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'container',
  data: {
    nodes: [
      { id: 'a', data: { label: 'A' } },
      { id: 'b', data: { label: 'B' } },
    ],
    edges: [{ id: 'a-b', source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
  },
  node: {
    type: 'circle',
    style: {
      size: 24,
      fill: '#1783FF',
      labelText: (datum) => String(datum.data?.label ?? datum.id),
    },
  },
  edge: { type: 'line', style: { stroke: '#B8C2D1', endArrow: true } },
  layout: { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 },
  behaviors: ['zoom-canvas', 'drag-canvas', 'drag-element', 'click-select'],
});

await graph.render();
```

Equivalent G6Lite starting point:

```ts
import { Graph } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const graph = new Graph({
  container: 'container',
  data: {
    nodes: [
      { id: 'a', data: { label: 'A' } },
      { id: 'b', data: { label: 'B' } },
    ],
    edges: [{ id: 'a-b', source: 'a', target: 'b' }],
  },
  node: {
    type: 'circle',
    style: {
      size: 24,
      fill: '#1783FF',
      label: (node) => String(node.data?.label ?? node.id),
    },
  },
  edge: { type: 'line', style: { stroke: '#B8C2D1', endArrow: true } },
  layout: { type: 'force', linkDistance: 100 },
  behaviors: [
    { type: 'zoom-canvas', sensitivity: 1, minZoom: 0.1, maxZoom: 20 },
    'drag-canvas',
    'drag-node',
    'click-select',
  ],
});

await graph.render();
```

The immediate differences are `labelText` becoming `label`, `drag-element` becoming `drag-node`, and every node, edge, and extension style field needing validation against G6Lite package-root types.

## GraphOptions mapping [#graphoptions-mapping]

| Option                    | G6 v5                            | G6Lite migration                                                                                     |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `container`               | String or container              | String or `HTMLElement`                                                                              |
| `data`                    | nodes / edges / combos           | Same concepts, but G6Lite requires `nodes` and `edges` arrays to exist                               |
| `node` / `edge` / `combo` | Full element configuration       | All supported, but types, style fields, and extension mechanisms are not field-compatible            |
| `layout`                  | Built-in and custom layouts      | 14 built-ins plus registered layouts; validate algorithm options individually                        |
| `behaviors`               | Behavior names or objects        | Strings or objects; names and options are mapped below                                               |
| `transforms`              | Built-in and custom Transforms   | `process-parallel-edges` and registered Transforms are supported with a different lifecycle contract |
| `plugins`                 | Rich built-in and custom plugins | Registered Plugin lifecycle is supported; built-ins and ecosystem are currently smaller              |
| `theme`                   | Theme and palette system         | `light` / `dark` plus a limited `ThemeTokens` override surface; fields differ                        |
| `animation`               | General animation configuration  | No equivalent GraphOptions animation system                                                          |
| `width` / `height`        | Constructor options and resize   | Container-driven; use `graph.setSize(width, height)` at runtime                                      |
| renderer                  | Canvas / SVG / WebGL and others  | Fixed hybrid path: WebGL for nodes/edges, Canvas 2D for labels/combos                                |

`graph.updateOptions()` currently updates `node`, `edge`, and `theme` only. Do not assume G6 v5 `setOptions()` semantics for replacing Behaviors, Plugins, Transforms, or Layout. Use `setLayout()` for layouts and rebuild or update Graph through the documented lifecycle for other configuration changes.

## Data field mapping [#data-field-mapping]

| G6 v5 field              | G6Lite                                 | Notes                                                                                |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `GraphData.nodes`        | `GraphData.nodes`                      | Required; pass `[]` when empty                                                       |
| `GraphData.edges`        | `GraphData.edges`                      | Required                                                                             |
| `GraphData.combos`       | `GraphData.combos?`                    | Supported, but collapse, nesting, and runtime regrouping remain experimental in beta |
| `node.id`                | `node.id`                              | Required and unique                                                                  |
| `node.data`              | `node.data`                            | Store business fields here; do not rely on G6 v5 internal model fields               |
| `node.style`             | `options.node.style`                   | Move shared styles to GraphOptions and use functions for per-node mapping            |
| `node.states`            | `node.states`                          | Initial states are supported; mutate with runtime state APIs                         |
| `node.combo` / `comboId` | `node.comboId`                         | Normalize to `comboId`                                                               |
| `node.x` / `node.y`      | Same names                             | Initial coordinates when layout is omitted                                           |
| `edge.id`                | `edge.id?`                             | Keep a stable explicit id for state and update APIs                                  |
| `edge.source` / `target` | Same names                             | Must reference existing node ids                                                     |
| `edge.data`              | `edge.data`                            | Business fields consumed by functional style mapping                                 |
| `combo.parentId`         | `combo.parentId`                       | Defines nested combos                                                                |
| `combo.style`            | `combo.style` or `options.combo.style` | Per-combo overrides and global configuration are both supported                      |

Nodes in the initial `GraphData` may omit coordinates when a layout is configured. Runtime `addNode()` requires `x` and `y`; migrate bulk creation to one `setData()` plus layout, or calculate coordinates before calling `addNode(s)`.

## Node, Edge, and Combo configuration [#node-edge-and-combo-configuration]

G6Lite builds in `circle` and `rect` nodes and `line`, `arc`, `polyline`, and `cubic` edges. `NodeConfig.type` and `EdgeConfig.type` also accept registered names, but custom extensions reuse built-in WebGL primitives and overlays rather than arbitrary G6 scene-graph shape trees.

Common mappings:

* Node text: migrate G6 v5 `labelText` to G6Lite `node.style.label`.
* Node size: use `size` for circles; rectangles can use `width`, `height`, and `borderRadius`.
* Edge arrows: use `startArrow`, `endArrow`, and `arrowSize`.
* Edge curves: do not copy quadratic and other type names blindly; choose `arc`, `cubic`, or `polyline` and configure `curvature`, `curveOffset`, `radius`, or `router`.
* Labels: node and edge labels support backgrounds, font styling, and placement; register a `label` extension for complex drawing instead of reaching into internal Canvas layers.
* State styles: use `node.stateStyles` and `edge.stateStyles`; combo state styles live under `combo.style.stateStyles`.
* Parallel edges: enable `edge.parallelEdges` or the `process-parallel-edges` Transform.

Combo declaration, nesting, collapse, runtime regrouping, states, and group drag are supported. See [Combo](/en/docs/guides/combo) and discard older migration notes that claimed G6Lite had no Combo support.

## Behavior mapping [#behavior-mapping]

| Common G6 v5 Behavior | G6Lite                | Migration note                                                                                                    |
| --------------------- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zoom-canvas`         | `zoom-canvas`         | Same name and G6-style delta-percentage `sensitivity`; G6Lite also batches per frame and caps each frame at 15%   |
| `drag-canvas`         | `drag-canvas`         | Same name; enabled with zoom when behaviors is omitted                                                            |
| `drag-element`        | `drag-node`           | Drags nodes and also drags a hit Combo as a group                                                                 |
| `click-select`        | `click-select`        | Single/multi-select options are supported; rebind payload types                                                   |
| `hover-activate`      | `hover-highlight`     | `highlight-node` and `highlight-edge` are also available                                                          |
| `brush-select`        | `brush-select`        | Shift/ctrl trigger options are supported                                                                          |
| `lasso-select`        | `lasso-select`        | Shift/ctrl trigger options are supported                                                                          |
| `collapse-expand`     | No same-name Behavior | Call `collapseCombo()`, `expandCombo()`, or `toggleCombo()`, or register an application Behavior                  |
| `create-edge`         | No direct equivalent  | `drag-edge` reconnects existing endpoints only; create a new edge in application interaction and call `addEdge()` |
| `focus-element`       | No same-name Behavior | Call `focusItem()` from the application event handler                                                             |
| `shortcuts-call`      | No same-name Behavior | Use the application shortcut layer or a custom Behavior                                                           |

The current 11 built-ins are `zoom-canvas`, `drag-canvas`, `highlight-node`, `highlight-edge`, `hover-highlight`, `drag-node`, `click-select`, `drag-edge`, `brush-select`, `lasso-select`, and `tooltip`.

When `behaviors` is omitted entirely, G6Lite enables `zoom-canvas` and `drag-canvas`. Passing `behaviors: []` disables those defaults. This differs from migration code that treats an empty list as “use defaults.”

## Layout migration [#layout-migration]

G6Lite currently supports `force`, `d3-force`, `force-atlas2`, `fruchterman`, `circular`, `concentric`, `radial`, `grid`, `dagre`, `mds`, `random`, `mindmap`, `indented`, and `fishbone`.

```ts
graph.setLayout({ type: 'dagre', rankdir: 'LR', nodesep: 40, ranksep: 80 });
await graph.layout();

// Starting another layout or destroying Graph also cancels the old run.
graph.cancelLayout();
```

Matching names do not guarantee matching options or defaults. Pin node size, center, direction, iteration limits, and link distance, then compare each layout on real data. Large graphs can try `worker: true`, while still reporting layout and rendering-only time separately.

Custom layouts use `register('layout', name, extensionFactory(...))`, implement `init → execute → destroy`, and respond to `AbortSignal` in long-running work. This is not a direct copy of a G6 v5 `BaseLayout` subclass.

## Event migration [#event-migration]

G6Lite does not export `NodeEvent`, `EdgeEvent`, `CanvasEvent`, `ComboEvent`, or `GraphEvent` enums. Use string event names and derive exact payloads from `GraphEventMap`.

```ts
import type { GraphEventMap } from '@antv/g6-lite';

const onNodeClick = ({ nodeId, data, nativeEvent }: GraphEventMap['node:click'][0]) => {
  console.log(nodeId, data, nativeEvent.clientX);
};

graph.on('node:click', onNodeClick);
graph.once('afterrender', ({ nodeCount, edgeCount }) => console.log(nodeCount, edgeCount));
graph.off('node:click', onNodeClick);
```

Common names still include `node:click`, `edge:click`, `canvas:click`, `afterrender`, and `afterlayout`, but do not reuse G6 v5 payload types. Node events expose `nodeId`; edge events expose `edgeId`, `edgeIndex`, `source`, and `target`; combo events expose `comboId`; and the original event is `nativeEvent`. Selection, drag, brush, and lasso derived events are emitted only when the matching Behavior is active.

## Graph API mapping [#graph-api-mapping]

| Common G6 v5 API                  | G6Lite                                                              | Difference                                                |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `render()` / `draw()`             | `render()`                                                          | Returns `Promise<void>`                                   |
| `getData()`                       | `getData()` / `toData()`                                            | Reads current graph data                                  |
| `setData(data)`                   | `await setData(data, options?)`                                     | Optional `fitView` controls the post-replacement viewport |
| `getNodeData(id?)`                | `getNodeData(id)` / `getNodes()`                                    | Single and list queries are separate                      |
| `getEdgeData(id?)`                | `getEdgeData(id)` / `getEdges()`                                    | Single and list queries are separate                      |
| `getElementData(id)`              | `getElementData(id)`                                                | Returns a read-only node, edge, or combo model            |
| `addNodeData()`                   | `addNode()` / `addNodes()`                                          | Runtime nodes require coordinates                         |
| `updateNodeData()`                | `updateNodeData()` / `updateNodePosition(s)`                        | Business data and coordinates are separate                |
| `removeNodeData()`                | `removeNode()` / `removeNodes()`                                    | Connected edges are handled                               |
| `addEdgeData()`                   | `addEdge()` / `addEdges()`                                          | Prefer stable explicit edge ids                           |
| `updateEdgeData()`                | `updateEdgeData()`                                                  | Can update data, source, and target                       |
| `removeEdgeData()`                | `removeEdge()` / `removeEdges()`                                    | Addressed by edge id                                      |
| `setElementState()`               | `setElementStates()` or `setItemState()`                            | Replace a state array or toggle one state                 |
| `getElementState()`               | `getItemStates()`                                                   | Returns a state array                                     |
| Query by state                    | `findNodesByState()` / `findEdgesByState()` / `findCombosByState()` | Returns id arrays                                         |
| `hideElement()` / `showElement()` | `hideItem()` / `showItem()`                                         | Different names                                           |
| `focusElement()`                  | `focusItem()`                                                       | Accepts one id or an id array                             |
| `fitView()` / `fitCenter()`       | Same names                                                          | `fitView` accepts padding, minZoom, and maxZoom           |
| `getZoom()` / `zoomTo()`          | Same names plus `zoomBy()`                                          | Optional center keeps a screen point fixed                |
| Camera API                        | `getCamera()` / `setCamera()` / `resetCamera()`                     | Direct camera management                                  |
| `resize()`                        | `setSize()`                                                         | Update container CSS dimensions as well                   |
| `setLayout()` / `layout()`        | Same names plus `cancelLayout()`                                    | Layout execution is cancellable                           |
| `setOptions()`                    | `updateOptions()`                                                   | Updates node, edge, and theme only                        |
| `destroy()` / destroyed           | `destroy()` / `destroyed` / `isDestroyed()`                         | Public APIs have defined destroyed-state safety           |

G6Lite also provides `batchSetState()`, `setElementStates(stateMap)`, neighbor and adjacent-edge queries, combo lifecycle APIs, and screen/graph coordinate conversion. Use the [API reference](/en/docs/api) and package-root types; do not create new dependencies on internal methods such as `getCanvas()` or low-level `updateData()` that are outside the reviewed package-root contract.

## Extension, Transform, and Plugin migration [#extension-transform-and-plugin-migration]

G6Lite supports eight categories: `node`, `edge`, `label`, `decoration`, `layout`, `behavior`, `transform`, and `plugin`. Use `extensionFactory()` for stateful instances:

```ts
import { extensionFactory, register } from '@antv/g6-lite';

register(
  'behavior',
  'business-select',
  extensionFactory(() => ({
    init(context) {
      // Keep the public ExtensionContext only.
    },
    getEvents() {
      return { 'node:click': ({ nodeId }) => console.log(nodeId) };
    },
    destroy() {},
  })),
);
```

Migration rules:

* Custom Node and Edge implementations do not inherit G6 scene-graph classes; use built-in primitives, functional styles, and controlled overlays.
* Label and Decoration Renderers own measurement and drawing only. The engine owns placement, rotation, collision, clipping, and refresh scheduling.
* Behavior, Transform, and Plugin code modifies Graph only through `ExtensionContext` data, state, viewport, and `requestRender()` capabilities.
* A Transform instance belongs to one Graph and one configuration position; a Plugin is created on mount and cleaned up on destroy. There is no public equivalent of G6 v5 `getPluginInstance()`.
* Extension failures are isolated and diagnosed. Do not access Renderer, DataModel, WebGL context, or deep source paths directly.

See [Extension system](/en/docs/guides/extensions) and [Custom Behavior](/en/docs/guides/custom-behavior).

## Unsupported capabilities and alternatives [#unsupported-capabilities-and-alternatives]

* **General animation orchestration**: keep the G6 v5 implementation or update data/camera over frames in application code; do not migrate the `animation` option blindly.
* **Complete graph algorithms**: run `@antv/algorithm` or another standalone algorithm package in application code, then write results into G6Lite data and states.
* **Multiple renderers, SSR, and 3D**: G6Lite Graph requires a real DOM, Canvas, and WebGL client lifecycle; prefer G6 v5 for these cases.
* **React/DOM nodes and arbitrary scene-graph shapes**: reduce the visual to G6Lite primitives and extension protocols, or keep that page on G6 v5.
* **Mature built-in plugins**: toolbar, minimap, history, and similar features require an application Plugin, external component, or retained G6 v5 implementation.
* **Unmapped Behaviors**: compose application events with Graph APIs or register a custom Behavior; do not use `drag-edge` as an edge-creation substitute.

## Migration acceptance checklist [#migration-acceptance-checklist]

1. Pin both library versions and keep the G6 v5 implementation as the rollback baseline.
2. Normalize data to explicit `nodes`, `edges`, and optional `combos`, preserving stable edge ids.
3. Migrate node, edge, and combo types, style functions, labels, arrows, and states field by field; drop unknown fields.
4. Replace Behaviors using the mapping and verify empty-list, default zoom, modifier-key, and derived-event semantics.
5. Rebind event payload types and verify nodeId, edgeId, comboId, coordinates, and nativeEvent.
6. Cover setData, mutations, batch state, visibility, focus, viewport, relayout, and destroy workflows.
7. Test lifecycle and error isolation for every custom element, Behavior, Transform, and Plugin.
8. Record layout, rendering-only, drag, zoom, picking, highlight, batch-update, and memory trends with real data.
9. Validate target browsers, DPR, GPU, CSP, and container sizes instead of relying on one development machine.
10. Remove the G6 v5 fallback only after visual, interaction, data-consistency, and performance acceptance all pass.

See the Playground `g6-v5-compat` demo for a runnable compatibility example and the [default theme example](/en/docs/examples/default-theme) for the visual state baseline.


# Compatibility overview (/en/docs/compatibility)



Review these boundaries before adopting or upgrading G6Lite:

<Cards>
  <Card title="Browsers and runtime" href="/en/docs/compatibility/browser" />

  <Card title="API stability" href="/en/docs/compatibility/api-stability" />

  <Card title="Graph library comparison" href="/en/docs/compatibility/library-comparison" />

  <Card title="Migrate from G6 v5" href="/en/docs/compatibility/g6-v5-migration" />
</Cards>

G6Lite needs a modern ESM browser, real DOM/Canvas, and WebGL 1.0. The package remains in `0.1.x` beta, and combo collapse, nesting, and runtime regrouping are experimental. Compare capability boundaries before selecting a library, then validate configuration, events, and runtime APIs during a G6 v5 migration.


# Graph library comparison (/en/docs/compatibility/library-comparison)



This page is a capability guide, not a performance ranking. Versions were checked on **2026-08-03**: G6Lite `0.1.0-beta.22`, AntV G6 `5.1.1`, sigma.js `3.0.3`, and Cytoscape.js `3.34.0`. Sigma v4 was still alpha, so the stable v3 line is used here.

Status terms: **Supported** means the core package or an official built-in capability can be used directly; **Partial** means clear boundaries apply; **External** means an official companion package, ecosystem extension, or application code is normally required; **Not supported** means the current public API has no equivalent.

## Short recommendation [#short-recommendation]

* **G6Lite** is a compact WebGL graph engine for products that need frequent picking, state, and incremental updates after a large graph is rendered and can work within a controlled extension surface.
* **AntV G6 v5** is a full graph visualization framework for rich elements, animation, components, plugins, multiple renderers, and the broader AntV ecosystem.
* **sigma.js v3** is a WebGL renderer built on Graphology, well suited to large-network exploration with existing coordinates or a separate layout pipeline.
* **Cytoscape.js** combines a graph-theory model with interactive visualization and fits applications that need graph queries, algorithms, mature extensions, and Node.js analysis.

## Rendering, data, and layout [#rendering-data-and-layout]

| Dimension                | G6Lite                                                                                         | AntV G6 v5                                                                                               | sigma.js v3                                                                            | Cytoscape.js                                                                        |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Rendering                | **Supported**: WebGL 2/1 for nodes and edges; Canvas 2D for labels and combos                  | **Supported**: AntV G renderers include Canvas, SVG, and WebGL, plus documented Node.js server rendering | **Supported**: WebGL renderer aimed at graphs with thousands of nodes and edges        | **Supported**: browser Canvas renderer; graph model can also run without a renderer |
| Data model               | **Supported**: `GraphData` and one Graph API with business `data` and states                   | **Supported**: complete graph and element model                                                          | **External**: Graphology is the required graph model                                   | **Supported**: built-in graph-theory model, collections, selectors, and queries     |
| Layouts                  | **Supported**: 14 layouts from AntV Layout plus mindmap, indented, and fishbone                | **Supported**: more than ten layouts and custom layout support                                           | **External**: normally Graphology layout packages, workers, or precomputed coordinates | **Supported**: core layouts plus a large layout-extension ecosystem                 |
| Worker / parallel layout | **Partial**: common layouts accept `worker: true`; custom layouts receive cancellation signals | **Supported**: official layout system includes parallel and extension options                            | **External**: Graphology layout workers or application infrastructure                  | **External**: depends on the selected layout extension                              |
| Incremental updates      | **Supported**: node, edge, state, visibility, and camera batch/incremental APIs                | **Supported**: complete runtime data and element update APIs                                             | **Supported**: renderer reacts to Graphology mutations                                 | **Supported**: collection mutations, batching, and style updates                    |

Layout time and rendering-only time must be measured separately. A sigma.js case that reuses coordinates cannot be fairly compared with another candidate that recomputes a force layout as part of first render.

## Elements, labels, and grouping [#elements-labels-and-grouping]

| Dimension             | G6Lite                                                                                                                 | AntV G6 v5                                                                      | sigma.js v3                                                                                                         | Cytoscape.js                                                         |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nodes                 | **Partial**: circle and rect built in; registered extensions reuse built-in primitives and overlays                    | **Supported**: rich built-in nodes, custom elements, and a React-node ecosystem | **Partial**: built-in node programs and custom WebGL programs                                                       | **Supported**: multiple shapes, mapped styles, and extensions        |
| Edges                 | **Partial**: line, arc, polyline, cubic, arrows, routing, parallel edges, and edge extensions                          | **Supported**: rich edge types, routing, decorations, and custom elements       | **Partial**: built-in edge programs and custom WebGL programs                                                       | **Supported**: multiple curves, arrows, endpoints, and mapped styles |
| Labels                | **Supported**: Canvas 2D labels, backgrounds, rotation, width limits, and custom Label Renderers                       | **Supported**: node, edge, and combo labels with rich styling                   | **Partial**: node labels are core; edge labels and advanced typography commonly require extensions or customization | **Supported**: node and edge labels with rich text styling           |
| Combo / compound node | **Partial**: declaration, nesting, collapse, regrouping, states, and group drag are supported but experimental in beta | **Supported**: complete Combo element and interaction ecosystem                 | **Not supported**: no equivalent visual group container in the core renderer                                        | **Supported**: compound nodes are part of the core model             |
| Visual states         | **Supported**: built-in/custom states, batching, state styles, queries, and visibility                                 | **Supported**: element states and interaction integration                       | **Partial**: commonly represented with Graphology attributes, reducers, and application state                       | **Supported**: classes, selectors, styles, and interaction state     |

G6Lite node and edge extensions preserve its WebGL batching primitives. They are not direct replacements for arbitrary G6 v5 Canvas/SVG scene-graph subclasses. Validate G6 v5 or Cytoscape.js first when the product requires arbitrary paths, complex DOM/React nodes, or a complete shape tree.

## Interaction, extension, and ecosystem [#interaction-extension-and-ecosystem]

| Dimension            | G6Lite                                                                                                               | AntV G6 v5                                                                                          | sigma.js v3                                                                                                       | Cytoscape.js                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Built-in interaction | **Supported**: 11 Behaviors for zoom, pan, drag, selection, highlight, brush, lasso, tooltip, and edge endpoint drag | **Supported**: more than ten Behaviors with a broader feature surface                               | **Partial**: camera, hover, click, and basic drag building blocks; editing is usually composed in the application | **Supported**: core gestures, selection, dragging, and events                                   |
| Custom interaction   | **Supported**: Behavior registration with `create → init → getEvents → destroy`                                      | **Supported**: BaseBehavior and registration system                                                 | **Supported**: events, camera, reducers, and application logic                                                    | **Supported**: event system, extensions, and application logic                                  |
| Extension categories | **Supported**: node, edge, label, decoration, layout, behavior, transform, plugin                                    | **Supported**: full element, Behavior, Layout, Transform, and Plugin system                         | **Partial**: custom programs, renderer settings, and the Graphology ecosystem                                     | **Supported**: layout, renderer, interaction, import/export, and analysis extensions            |
| Plugins              | **Partial**: public Plugin lifecycle exists, but built-ins and community ecosystem are still small                   | **Supported**: mature built-in and ecosystem plugins such as toolbar, minimap, tooltip, and history | **External**: community packages and framework integrations provide many product components                       | **Supported**: mature extension directory across layout, analysis, and UI                       |
| Animation            | **Partial**: no general Graph animation orchestration API; isolated element effects or extensions are possible       | **Supported**: element, layout, viewport, and transition animation system                           | **Partial**: camera and node-attribute animation utilities; complex timelines stay in application code            | **Supported**: element and viewport animation APIs                                              |
| Graph algorithms     | **Not supported**: neighbor and adjacent-edge queries only; no built-in shortest-path or centrality suite            | **Supported**: official package integrates `@antv/algorithm`                                        | **External**: use Graphology standard-library algorithm packages                                                  | **Supported**: traversal, shortest paths, centrality, connectivity, and other graph-theory APIs |

## Runtime and package shape [#runtime-and-package-shape]

| Dimension            | G6Lite                                                         | AntV G6 v5                                                               | sigma.js v3                                                                                               | Cytoscape.js                                                        |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Browser requirements | Modern ESM, real DOM/Canvas, and WebGL 1.0+                    | Depends on the selected renderer and build target                        | Modern browser with WebGL                                                                                 | Browser Canvas; can also run headless                               |
| Node.js / SSR        | **No rendering**: create Graph only in a client lifecycle      | **Supported**: official documentation describes Node.js server rendering | **Partial**: Graphology runs in Node.js, while the Sigma renderer still needs a browser/WebGL environment | **Supported**: graph model and algorithms run headlessly in Node.js |
| TypeScript           | Bundled types; package-root exports define the public contract | TypeScript source and complete types                                     | Bundled types                                                                                             | Type declarations included                                          |
| Maturity             | `0.1.x` beta with a controlled API surface and young ecosystem | Stable `5.1.1` with the broader AntV ecosystem                           | Stable `3.0.3`; v4 is alpha                                                                               | Stable `3.34.0` with long-running maintenance and extensions        |

## How to choose [#how-to-choose]

Prefer G6Lite when the target environment reliably supports WebGL; post-render picking, state, and batch updates are the main bottleneck; circle/rect nodes, common edge primitives, and controlled extensions cover the visual requirements; and SSR, a general animation system, and graph algorithms are not required.

Prefer G6 v5 when the product needs rich elements, the complete plugin and animation systems, multiple renderers, React nodes, 3D, or server-side rendering, and a broader capability surface matters more than the smallest runtime.

Prefer sigma.js when the team already uses Graphology, coordinates come from a backend or separate layout pipeline, and the main product workflow is browsing, filtering, and exploring large networks.

Prefer Cytoscape.js when graph-theory analysis, compound nodes, complex selectors, headless Node.js, and mature scientific/network-analysis extensions are central requirements.

## Fair validation checklist [#fair-validation-checklist]

1. Pin candidate versions, data, coordinates, styles, label policy, viewport, DPR, browser, and hardware.
2. Split preset-coordinate and relayout cases, and report layout versus rendering-only time separately.
3. Test drag, zoom, picking, highlighting, batch updates, and post-destroy memory trends in addition to first render.
4. Use realistic combos, labels, arrows, and state counts instead of bare points and lines only.
5. Record median, P95, sample count, and error, and archive the complete adapter and configuration.

See [performance metrics](/en/docs/metrics/performance) and [performance tuning](/en/docs/metrics/performance-tuning) for the G6Lite measurement workflow.

## Official sources [#official-sources]

* [AntV G6 README](https://github.com/antvis/G6#readme) and [G6 documentation](https://g6.antv.antgroup.com/)
* [sigma.js README](https://github.com/jacomyal/sigma.js#readme), [sigma.js documentation](https://www.sigmajs.org/docs/), and [Graphology](https://graphology.github.io/)
* [Cytoscape.js README](https://github.com/cytoscape/cytoscape.js#readme) and [Cytoscape.js documentation](https://js.cytoscape.org/)
